question: A linked list may loop back on itself, and you may use only a constant amount of extra memory. How can you tell whether it loops?
options: Count nodes until the count passes a big number
Run two pointers, one twice as fast; if they ever meet, it loops
Store every node you visit in a set
explanation: In a loop the faster pointer gains one node per step and must catch the slower one; without a loop it reaches the end. A set also works but uses O(n) memory, and a count limit can give the wrong answer.
